Rashi on Niddah 24b:10:1.hebrew: דמות לילית - שידה. שד יש לו פרצוף אדם, ויש לו כנפים:
Rashi on Niddah 24b:10:1.english: The form of a lilith - A female demon. A demon has a human face, and it has wings.

Rashi on Niddah 24b:11:1.hebrew: הנהג בן אחיך ובא - כלומר, הבא בן אחיך ובא עמו:
Rashi on Niddah 24b:11:1.english: Lead your nephew and come - That is to say: Bring your nephew, and come with him.

Rashi on Niddah 24b:12:1.hebrew: ה"ג: בהליכתן, יצתה כלת חנינא לקראת רבי יהושע:
Rashi on Niddah 24b:12:1.english: This is the reading: While they were going, Ḥanina's daughter-in-law went out to greet Rabbi Yehoshua.

Rashi on Niddah 24b:14:2.hebrew: המפלת סנדל - אין סנדל בלא ולד אחר, ובשביל סנדל תשב לזכר ולנקבה, דספק זכר ספק נקבה הוא. ואם הולד אחר נקבה, אין הסנדל לא מעלה ולא מוריד, ולא תשב אלא לנקבה ימי טומאה וימי טהרה, שאפי' הוא זכר — הואיל ונקבה בהדיה, לא בצירי ימי טומאתה וימי טהרה דנקבה, שהרי של זכר מובלעין בתוך של נקבה. וכי אצטריך תשב לזכר ולנקבה — כגון שהולד השני זכר, דיהבינן לה חומרת טומאה דנקבה בשביל הסנדל, וימי טוהר לזכר לחומרא:
Rashi on Niddah 24b:14:2.english: One who discharges a sandal - There is no sandal [fetus] without another offspring, and on account of the sandal she observes [the regulations] for a male and for a female, as it is uncertain whether it is a male or a female. And if the other offspring is a female, the sandal neither adds nor detracts, and she observes only [the regulations of] a female [regarding] the days of impurity and the days of purity; for even if it is a male, since a female is alongside it, the days of her impurity and the days of purity of a female are not diminished, as those of a male are subsumed within those of a female. And when it was necessary [to state that] "she observes for a male and for a female," [this is in a case] such as where the second offspring is a male, where we apply to her the stringency of a female's impurity on account of the sandal, and the days of purity of a male as a stringency.

Rashi on Niddah 24b:15:1.hebrew: שמא ולד היה ונימוח - כיון דלאו דם הוא ולאו מים נינהו, איכא למיחש לולד:
Rashi on Niddah 24b:15:1.english: Perhaps it was an offspring and it liquefied - Since it is not blood and it is not water, there is reason to be concerned for an offspring.

Rashi on Niddah 24b:15:2.english: How much undiluted wine, etc. - An expression of exaggeration.

Rashi on Niddah 24b:16:1.english: This is our reading: "Rava says: We learned 'full'."

Rashi on Niddah 24b:17:1.hebrew: סכויין - שחורין. שמעתי ל"א: סכויין - בלא מוח ומשיחה, אלא יבשה:
Rashi on Niddah 24b:17:1.english: Sekuyin - [They are] black. I heard another explanation: Sekuyin [means] without marrow and oiliness, but rather dry.

Rashi on Niddah 24b:18:1.english: A thighbone - The bone of the thigh.

Rashi on Niddah 24b:1:1.english: And Shmuel explains according to his reasoning - [Both] the first clause and the last clause [deal with a case] where it emerged into the airspace of the world.

Rashi on Niddah 24b:1:2.hebrew: דאע"ג דכלו לו חדשיו - נפל הוא, דלא חיי, ונבלה הואי:
Rashi on Niddah 24b:1:2.english: Even though its months were completed - It is a non-viable birth, for it cannot live, and it is a carcass.

Rashi on Niddah 24b:21:1.english: The attendant - An attendant of the Sages, and Adda was his name.

Rashi on Niddah 24b:2:1.hebrew: שאינו חתוך - כולו שלם כעין דף, ואין בו חיתוך אברים וצורה, אלא חלק כעין עיגול:
Rashi on Niddah 24b:2:1.english: That is not articulated - It is entirely whole like a board, and has no articulation of limbs or features, but rather is smooth like a circle.

Rashi on Niddah 24b:2:2.hebrew: וטמאה שבעת ימים וביום השמיני ימול - משמע: מי שהוא ראוי לחיות שמנה ימים, אמו טמאה לידה; ומי שאינו ראוי לחיות שמנה לברית — לא:
Rashi on Niddah 24b:2:2.english: And she shall be impure seven days, and on the eighth day he shall be circumcised - [This] implies that [for] one who is fit to live eight days, his mother is impure [with the impurity of] childbirth; but [for] one who is not fit to live eight [days] for circumcision, [she is] not.

Rashi on Niddah 24b:3:1.hebrew: א"ל רב - לתנא: סיים בה נמי הכי, ואימא: יצאו אלו, מי שיש לו שני גבין וכו':
Rashi on Niddah 24b:3:1.english: Rav said to him - To the tanna: Conclude it also like this, and say: "Excluded are these: one who has two backs, etc."

Rashi on Niddah 24b:4:1.hebrew: כוותיה דשמואל - בשני גבין, דולד הוא, וקאמר: טמאה אפילו בלידה יבישתא, דולד הוא:
Rashi on Niddah 24b:4:1.english: In accordance with Shmuel - In [the case of a fetus with] two backs, that it is [considered] an offspring, and he said [that she is] impure even in [the case of] a dry birth, since it is an offspring.

Rashi on Niddah 24b:5:1.hebrew: הרי אמרו אשה יולדת לט' ויולדת לז' - ואנא נמי אמינא: כי היכי דבהמה לט', כדאמרי' לעיל בן ח' לגסה נפל, הכא נמי: יולדת לז' נפל, או לאו נפל הוא ומותר:
Rashi on Niddah 24b:5:1.english: Behold, they said: A woman gives birth at nine and gives birth at seven - And I [Rava] also say: Just as an animal [normally gives birth] at nine [months] — as we said above, an eight-month [fetus] of large livestock is a non-viable birth — here too, [does an animal that] gives birth at seven [produce a] non-viable birth, or is it not a non-viable birth, and [thus] permitted?

Rashi on Niddah 24b:6:1.english: From this and below - It is taught in the baraita above.

Rashi on Niddah 24b:6:2.hebrew: מאי לאו אגסה - נמי קאי, דקתני בן ח' לגסה, והימנו ולמטה, כגון בר ז', אסור:
Rashi on Niddah 24b:6:2.english: What, is it not [referring] to large [livestock] - It also applies [to large livestock], for [the baraita] teaches: "An eight-month-old for large [livestock], and from it and below" — such as a seven-month-old — "is forbidden."

Rashi on Niddah 24b:6:3.hebrew: אדקה - בן ד' לדקה והימנו ולמטה, כגון בר תלתא, אסור:
Rashi on Niddah 24b:6:3.english: To a small animal - A four-month-old for a small animal, and from it and below, such as a three-month-old, is forbidden.

Rashi on Niddah 24b:8:1.hebrew: אלא אי אמרת אדקה פשיטא - הואיל ובר תלתא הוא, לא חיי:
Rashi on Niddah 24b:8:1.english: Rather, if you say [it was stated] regarding a small [animal], it is obvious - Since it is [a fetus of] three [months], it does not survive.

Rashi on Niddah 24b:9:1.hebrew: כל בציר תרי ירחי - מכדרכו חיי, כי היכי דבאשה ובבהמה גסה בר ז' חיי, דהוי תרי ירחי בציר מכי אורחיה, הכי נמי בר תלתא לדקה חיי, אע"ג דבר ד' לא חיי:
Rashi on Niddah 24b:9:1.english: Any [fetus born] two months less - Than its normal [gestation period] survives. Just as with a woman and a large animal, [one born at] seven [months] survives, which is two months less than its normal [period], so too, [one born at] three [months] for a small [animal] survives, even though [one born at] four [months] does not survive.

Rashi on Niddah 24b:9:2.english: It teaches us - That it does not survive.

Tosafot on Niddah 24b:10:1.hebrew: המפלת דמות לילית אמו טמאה לידה - וא"ת: פשיטא, מי גרע מגופו תיש ופניו אדם, דהוי ולד לכ"ע? וי"ל, דהתם יצא מתורת בהמה והוי אדם, והכא לא יצא כלל מתורת לילית. אך ק"ק, דאמרי' לעיל (נדה כג.) בעופות תבדק לרבנן, דקריא וקיפופא הוי ולד, אף על גב דלסתות לא מפיק ליה כלל מתורת כוס וינשוף. וי"ל, שמואל דהכא יפרש לעיל: תבדק לר"מ:
Tosafot on Niddah 24b:10:1.english: A woman who discharges the likeness of a lilith, its mother is impure [with the impurity of] childbirth - And if you say: It is obvious! Is it any worse than [one whose] body is [that of] a goat and whose face is [that of] a human, which is [considered] an offspring according to everyone? And one can say: There, it departed from the category of an animal and is [considered] a human, whereas here, it did not depart at all from the category of a lilith. However, it is slightly difficult, as we say above (Niddah 23a) that "in [the case of] birds, it must be examined" [applies] according to the Rabbis, [and] that a little owl (karya) and a great owl (kifofa) are [considered] an offspring, even though [having] cheeks does not remove it at all from the category of a kos (little owl) and a yanshuf (great owl). And one can say: Shmuel here would explain [the statement] above, "it must be examined," [as being] according to Rabbi Meir.

Tosafot on Niddah 24b:14:1.hebrew: המפלת סנדל או שליא תשב לזכר ולנקבה - וא"ת: בשליא ליתני נמי ולנדה, דאימא הרחיקה לידתה וכבר כלו ימי טוהר, כדאיתא לקמן בפירקין (נדה דף כח.) גבי המפלת יד חתוכה; אע"ג דאמר בסמוך אין תולין השליא בולד יותר מג' ימים, להחמיר חוששין יותר מג' ימים. וי"ל, דלא דמו: דבהמפלת יד חתוכה איכא למימר דהראש או רוב הגוף כבר ילדה מקודם וכלו ימי טוהר, אבל שליא אימא הולד בתוכה, או שלם או נימוק. ועוד י"ל, דאי הוה תני ולנדה, ה"א מביאה קרבן ואינו נאכל, דספק לידה היא; קמ"ל מביאה קרבן ונאכל. והכי נמי קאמר לקמן:
Tosafot on Niddah 24b:14:1.english: A woman who discharges a sandal or an afterbirth shall observe [the strictures of] a male and a female - And if you say: In [the case of] an afterbirth, let [the Tanna] also teach "and [the strictures of] a niddah" — for say that her childbirth was in the distant past and the days of purity have already ended, as is stated later in our chapter (Niddah 28a) regarding one who discharges a severed hand; [and] even though [the Gemara] says nearby that we do not attribute the afterbirth to an offspring [born] more than three days [prior], to be stringent we should suspect [that the birth occurred] more than three days [ago]! And one can answer that they are not comparable: For in [the case of] one who discharges a severed hand, it can be said that she had already given birth to the head or the majority of the body previously and the days of purity have ended; but [in the case of] an afterbirth, say that the offspring is inside it, either intact or dissolved. And furthermore, one can answer that if [the Tanna] had taught "and [the strictures of] a niddah", I would say that she brings an offering and it is not eaten, because it is an uncertain childbirth; [therefore,] it teaches us that she brings an offering and it is eaten. And so too does [the Gemara] say later.

Tosafot on Niddah 24b:17:1.hebrew: אכילתו מרובה משתייתו - פי' יותר מדאי מרובה על השתיה, דהא דרך אכילה להיות מרובה על השתיה, כדאמרי' בפ"ק דמגילה (דף יב.): והשתיה כדת אין אונס — כדת של תורה, דאכילה מרובה משתייה, דקרבנות יש יותר מנסכים. והא דאמרי' בערבי פסחים (דף קי.) ובגיטין (דף ע.): אכול שליש ושתה שליש והנח שליש, לכשתכעוס תעמוד על מילואך — לאו דוקא, אלא שבין אכילה ושתיה יהיו שני שלישים:
Tosafot on Niddah 24b:17:1.english: One whose eating exceeds his drinking - This means [that his eating] excessively exceeds drinking, for it is normal for eating to exceed drinking, as we say in the first chapter of Megillah (12a): "And the drinking was according to the law; none did compel" (Esther 1:8) — according to the law of the Torah, [where] eating exceeds drinking, as there are more sacrifices than libations. And as for that which we say in Arvei Pesachim (110a) and in Gittin (70a): "Eat a third, and drink a third, and leave a third [empty], so that when you become angry you will reach your full capacity" — [this] is not exact; rather, between eating and drinking [combined] there should be two thirds.

Tosafot on Niddah 24b:3:1.english: One who is fit for the creation of a soul - And some read: "for circumcision on the eighth [day]."
